summary: CLI exposes host to remote shell/file/PTY commands from hardcoded AppSync backend
details: When the operator runs `ai-support-agent start`, the CLI opens a persistent AWS AppSync WebSocket to api.ai-support-agent.com and subscribes for `agent-command` notifications. Each notification is fetched via `client.getCommand()` and dispatched through `executeCommand` to handlers including `execute_command` (spawns `/bin/sh -c <payload.command>`), `file_read`/`file_write`/`file_delete`/`file_rename`/`file_mkdir`, `process_kill`, `ssh_exec`, and `server_setup_exec` — the remote party supplies the shell command, file paths, and content. Separately, `TerminalWebSocket` connects to `/ws/agent-terminal` on the configured API and pipes remote `stdin` frames (base64-decoded) directly into a `node-pty` bash/zsh (optionally under tmux) spawned per remote `open` message; the remote peer also controls resize and session create/kill. dist/cli/service/darwin-service.js and linux-service.js install the CLI as a persistent user service (launchd/systemd with PATH setup), so the WebSocket-to-shell surface can run under a long-lived service context. The result is that any party in control of the AppSync tenant/token or the API host can execute arbitrary shell commands, read/write arbitrary files, and drive an interactive PTY on any machine running the CLI, whether or not that is the advertised product behavior.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
